db_evidence.notes: episodes/object_states captions unambiguously place a 'someone hands him a white real madrid jersey marked ronaldo 7' event at 282741-282771s (before boarding the tram) and a 'peels a banana' event at 283971-284001s (while riding). No episode/topic_fact/object_state caption in the logical clue window [283369,283950] or its immediate surroundings mentions tissue, napkin, or paper being received; the only DB-indexed tissue/napkin event near this timeframe is at 172188-172218s on a visually distinct red-seated bus (an unrelated earlier scene). One rollout's clip_qa (rollout 2) visually located a plausible tissue/paper hand-through-window event at ~283905s, after the jersey and roughly contemporaneous with/just before the banana at ~283953s. Across all 5 independent rollouts and manual frame checks, no evidence anywhere places a banana handoff before the jersey (jersey is the earliest-appearing item by ~900-1200s in every account). This directly contradicts the reference answer '3,1,2' (banana first, then jersey, then tissue).

root_causes: The reference answer's ordering (banana, jersey, tissue) is not supported by DB captions, semantic-triple/object-state text, or five independent visual (clip_qa) inspections, all of which place the jersey handoff clearly first (~282763, before boarding) and the banana handling last (~283950-284001); this looks like a reference-answer/ground-truth error rather than a retrieval failure by the agent.

The 'tissue paper' item is genuinely hard to locate: it is either absent from automatic captions in the relevant window or only visible transiently (~283905s) via close visual inspection, causing rollouts to either miss it, misattribute it to an unrelated earlier bus (172188s), or (rollout 3) have clip_qa hallucinate an incorrect jersey+tissue pair at 283734-283744 that contradicts the actual frame content.

Because every rollout's honestly-retrieved evidence contradicts the fixed reference ordering, no amount of correct retrieval could produce a score above partial credit; the low/zero scores reflect a judge scoring against a likely-incorrect reference rather than agent retrieval failure.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly and consistently located the jersey handoff event (~282741-282801) and the banana-eating event (~283971-284001) via semantic_search + run_sql + clip_qa triangulation.

Several rollouts (0, 1) correctly identified and rejected an out-of-scene tissue/napkin candidate at 172188s as belonging to a different (red-seated) bus rather than blindly accepting a lexical match.
Rollout 4 achieved partial credit by reporting only the two items it could visually confirm (jersey, banana) rather than fabricating a third.
transferable_lessons: When a proposed answer's item ordering contradicts every independently retrieved timestamp by a wide margin (here, ~900-1200s), flag the mismatch explicitly and consider that the reference/expected labeling may itself be wrong, rather than searching indefinitely for a hidden confirming event.

Cross-validate a single clip_qa call's claimed timestamp against the corresponding stored episode/object_state caption for that exact interval before trusting it; rollout 3's clip_qa asserted a jersey handoff at 283734 that the stored caption ('tossing objects toward a crowd... don't throw it') and a manually pulled frame both contradict.

For 'received from fans on vehicle X' style questions, first establish the entry/boarding timestamp precisely (it anchors what counts as 'on the bus' vs 'before boarding'), since agents disagreed on whether the jersey handoff (which occurred outside, before boarding) counts as happening 'on the bus'.

Small object hand-offs (tissue, small paper items) are frequently under-captioned by the automatic pipeline; when a caption-only search returns nothing, a dedicated clip_qa scan across the full candidate window (not just at anchor points) can surface a real but faint event.
